description: In **1889**, from the asylum of Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, **Vincent Van Gogh** painted *The Starry Night*. The sky swirls: art stops copying reality to express an emotion.

hero.hook: From an asylum room, Van Gogh paints a sky that refuses to remain wise.

blocks.text: *The Starry Night* (**1889**) is the most famous painting by **Vincent Van Gogh**, painter born in . Painted at the Saint-Rémy-de-Provence asylum, it marks a turning point: we no longer paint only what we see. We paint what we feel. [[Netherlands]]
Swirling sky, cypress like a black flame, invented village: the work opens the way to the expressive art of the 20th century.

In **May 1889**, after the [[Drama of Arles with Gauguin]] (the crisis which cost him part of his ear), Van Gogh was interned in **Saint-Paul-de-Mausole**, near Saint-Rémy. He gets a room to paint. The nocturnal view is first born behind the bars of his room.

blocks.caption: The Saint-Rémy asylum: framework of constraint and intense creation.

blocks.text: The canvas mixes observation and invention. We recognize the hills of the Alpilles and a large **cypress**. But the village is not an exact copy. Van Gogh reconstructs the landscape to serve emotion.
Technically, Van Gogh uses **Impasto**: the paint is thick, almost sculpted. Eleven stars rotate like nebulae. The orange moon radiates. The sky becomes the real character.

blocks.caption: The cypress connects the earth to the sky like a dark flame.

blocks.text: The large scrolls of the sky recall the dynamics of , a Japanese print that Van Gogh admired. It transforms this energy into cosmos. [[The Great Wave off Kanagawa]]
This gesture announces the [[Art as inner expression]]: the canvas says a state of mind, not a weather report.

sections.title: Sculpting the sky with a brush

blocks.text: Van Gogh painted nearly **900 paintings** in ten years, but died in **July 1890** in Auvers-sur-Oise, at **37 years**, almost unknown. It was his sister-in-law, **Johanna van Gogh-Bonger**, who saved the work: exhibitions, sales, publication of letters to his brother Théo.

*The Starry Night* changed hands several times for little money, before entering the **MoMA** in New York. The despised painting becomes an icon. The [[Fauves]], painters with violent colors from the beginning of the 20th century, will recognize in him an ancestor.

sections.title: The genius that no one bought

blocks.text: The cypress connects the ground to the sky: a link between earthly life and elsewhere. Van Gogh wrote that looking at the stars made him dream of death like a journey. Modern studies even suggest that the bright star near the cypress tree could be Venus, observed at dawn.

blocks.text: *Starry Night* transforms suffering into visual language. Van Gogh does not copy the night: he invents an interior sky, and opens the door to modern expressive art.
